output.scope_note: The paper is an MD study of Li-ion transport in the solid cathode Li3TiCl6 and reports ionic conductivity values, one computed in this work and one cited from the experimental reference.

records.measurement_method: DLMD (deep learning molecular dynamics) with Nernst-Einstein relation
records.evidence_quote: Ionic conductivity (1.06 mS/cm) and activation energy (0.29eV) calculated by our simulation are highly comparable with that of experimental values.
records.notes: Simulated conductivity from this paper's MLFF-MD (Nernst-Einstein with Haven ratio). The abstract does not state a temperature for this value; the paper's simulations span 298-373 K, so no temperature is assigned. Activation energy 0.29 eV is the paper's own DLMD result.

records.evidence_quote: which represents experimentally annealed structure at 300o C and exhibited a maximum Li-ion conductivity of 1.04 mS/cm at room temperature[13]
records.notes: Experimental value from Ref. [13] (Wang et al., Nat. Commun. 2023), cited in this paper, not measured here. The 300 C annealing refers to the experimental structure in Ref. [13]. The experimental activation energy of 0.32 eV is also cited but is not a conductivity, so it is not recorded.
